model_answer: A transient error is retried after a wait that grows: half a second, then one, then two, never above the cap. Each wait is a random share of that, so clients do not retry together. Each wait is a retry_wait line, and a failed call is a model_error line. After three failed calls in a row the breaker opens, the trace gets a breaker line, and the run ends with circuit_open instead of retrying forever.

model_answer: A real-time test waits for every backoff, so an eight-second wait costs eight seconds, and a suite of retry tests becomes slow enough that people stop running it. On a virtual clock sleep() only moves time forward, so the test runs at once. The seeded random source makes the waits repeat exactly, so the test checks the same numbers on every run.
prompt: Why should a test of retries run on a virtual clock, and what would a real-time test cost?
rubric: Says a real-time test waits for every wait it tests
Says the virtual clock moves forward without waiting
Says the seeded random source makes the waits repeat
